attributes.body_ja:
「序（つい）でに」は、「(A) の機会（きかい）に、別（べつ）の (B) をする」という意味（いみ）で使（つか）われる副詞（ふくし）です。「序（つい）で」はもともと名詞（めいし）で、「順番（じゅんばん）」などの意味（いみ）を持（も）っています。そのため、この文法（ぶんぽう）には「(A) が本来（ほんらい）の目的（もくてき）で、(B) はその機会（きかい）を利用（りよう）してする追加（ついか）の行動（こうどう）」というニュアンスがあります。また、実際（じっさい）の行動（こうどう）も、(A) → (B) の順番（じゅんばん）になります。

「序（つい）でに」はふつう、動詞（どうし）や名詞（めいし）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われます。名詞（めいし）の場合（ばあい）は、その前（まえ）に「の」を付（つ）ける必要（ひつよう）があります。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「序（つい）でに」は、特（とく）に急（いそ）ぎではないけれど、(A) をするなら (B) も一緒（いっしょ）にやってしまうと都合（つごう）がいいような場面（ばめん）でよく使（つか）われます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「序（つい）でに」は、「間（あいだ）に」や「時（とき）に」と比べると、何度（なんど）も繰（く）り返（かえ）す行動（こうどう）よりも、一度（いちど）だけの行動（こうどう）に使（つか）われやすい表現（ひょうげん）です。ただし、主（おも）な目的（もくてき）に追加（ついか）して行（おこな）うことであれば、何度（なんど）も行（おこな）うことに使（つか）われることもあります。また、一度（いちど）だけの行動（こうどう）の場合（ばあい）は、いつもはしないことだったり、(A) と一緒（いっしょ）にたまたまできることだったりする行動（こうどう）であることが多（おお）いです。
attributes.body:
序（つい）でに is an adverb in Japanese that is used in a similar way to 'while you're at it', or 'on the occasion of (A)' in English. 序（つい）で itself is a noun that means 'precedence' (in terms of being the first thing to happen). Due to this, the literal meaning of 序（つい）でに may be thought of as 'with (A) as the precedence, (B)'.

序（つい）でに is commonly used with verbs, or nouns. In the case of nouns, it will need to be preceded by the case marking particle の.

Fun Fact

Just like 'precedence' in English, 序（つい）でに implies that (A) is the instigator for (B). Because of this, 序（つい）でに is a good way to convey that something is not urgent, but, if (A) is happening, it is the perfect chance to do (B) as well.

Caution

Compared to 間（あいだ）に and 時（とき）に, 序（つい）でに has more of a tendency to be used for incidental 'one-off' things, rather than regular occurrences. Despite this, it still may be used to describe regular occurrences at times. However, these one-off occurrences are likely to have the nuance of being something slightly irregular, coincidental, or requiring effort; rather than something that requires no effort or can be achieved in moments.

attributes.description: How to use ついでに

attributes.body: ついでに and の間に can both express the idea of 'while', but are used in different contexts. ついでに implies taking advantage of one action to do another, e.g. 買い物のついでに銀行に寄った ('I stopped by the bank while shopping.') の間に, by contrast, means 'during/while (A), (B)' without the added nuance of 'while you're at it' that comes with ついでに.

first_relatable.title: ついでに
first_relatable.meaning: While you are at it, On the occasion

attributes.body: Both ついでに and つつ involve performing multiple actions together, but differ in nuance. ついでに expresses performing a second action while it's convenient or appropriate, e.g. '買い物のついでに郵便局に寄った' ('I stopped at the post office while shopping'). つつ is a formal expression indicating simultaneous actions or states, e.g. 'レシピを見つつ料理をする' ('cook while looking at a recipe').

attributes.body: Both ついでに and ～ところに・～ところへ relate to timing, but from different angles. ついでに expresses performing a second action while it's convenient, e.g. '買い物のついでに郵便局に寄った' ('I stopped at the post office while shopping'). ～ところに・～ところへ focuses on when something happens, often unexpectedly, e.g. '出かけようとしたところに電話がかかってきた' ('Just as I was about to leave, the phone rang').

attributes.body: Both connect actions to a larger context, but with different emphasis. ついでに expresses performing a second action while it's convenient, e.g. '買い物のついでに郵便局に寄った' ('I stopped at the post office while shopping'). にあたり・にあたって is more formal and used for actions on a certain occasion, e.g. '開会にあたり、ご挨拶申し上げます' ('On the occasion of the opening, I extend my greetings').

attributes.body: ついでに and がけに both relate to doing something while engaged in another action. ついでに expresses a second action done while convenient, e.g. '買い物のついでに郵便局に寄った' ('I stopped at the post office while shopping'). がけに is used with movement verbs and emphasizes doing something during a transition, e.g. '帰りがけに電話した' ('I called on my way home').

attributes.body: Both express simultaneous actions, but differ in nuance. ついでに implies convenience, e.g. '買い物のついでに郵便局に寄った' ('I stopped at the post office while shopping'). がてら implies doing something while moving, e.g. '散歩がてら郵便を出した' ('I mailed a letter while taking a walk'). They also differ grammatically: がてら connects directly to nouns, while ついでに requires の.

attributes.body: Both can be translated as 'while', but with different implications. ついでに means 'while you're at it' and adds a convenient extra action, e.g. 買い物のついでに銀行に寄った ('I stopped by the bank while shopping.') うちに emphasizes doing something before a condition changes, e.g. 熱いうちに食べてね ('Eat it while it's hot.')

first_relatable.title: ついでに
first_relatable.meaning: While you are at it, On the occasion

attributes.body: Both ついでに and 際に refer to additional actions tied to another event, but differ in tone. ついでに is an everyday expression for when something is done while convenient, e.g. '買い物のついでに郵便局に寄った' ('I stopped at the post office while shopping'). 際に is more formal and emphasizes a particular occasion, e.g. '来日の際にご連絡ください' ('Please contact us when you come to Japan').

attributes.body: Both can mean 'while,' but the nuance differs. ついでに implies doing something extra during another task, e.g. 買い物のついでに郵便局に寄った ('While shopping, I stopped at the post office.'). ているあいだに just marks that something happened during another action, as in 買い物しているあいだに電話がかかってきた ('I got a call while shopping.').

first_relatable.title: ついでに
first_relatable.meaning: While you are at it, On the occasion

attributes.body: ながら attaches to verb stems to express performing one action simultaneously with another, e.g. 音楽を聴きながら走る 'listen to music while running'. In contrast, ついでに follows various words or phrases to convey the idea of taking advantage of the opportunity to do another thing at the same time, e.g. 買い物に行くついでに走ってきた ('On the occasion of going shopping, I went for a run.').

second_relatable.title: ついでに
second_relatable.meaning: While you are at it, On the occasion

attributes.body: ているところだ and ついでに both relate to ongoing actions but differ greatly in usage. ているところだ describes an action in progress at that moment, with the nuance that the speaker is currently occupied (e.g. 昼ご飯を食べているところだ = 'I'm in the middle of eating lunch'). In contrast, ついでに describes performing an 'extra' action on the same occasion as another (e.g. 散歩のついでに昼ご飯を買ってきた = 'While on a walk, I bought lunch').
